brief: A habit tracker as a garden — daily completion waters plants, streaks bloom, neglect wilts

dominant_strengths: Strong metaphor: sky-and-soil split with plants-as-habits is immediately legible and emotionally warm
Concept has clear systemic logic — water, bloom, wilt states map cleanly to streaks, completion, neglect
Color palette (sky blue to earth brown gradient) feels native to the garden idea without being saccharine
dominant_weaknesses: Massive empty sky wastes 60% of the canvas; plants are tiny stems crammed at the bottom edge
Plant illustrations are crude line-and-dot primitives, undermining the 'bloom' payoff that should be visceral
Stats card overlaps and obscures two plants, breaking the garden composition and signaling poor layout hierarchy
fix_priorities: Rebalance vertical composition — raise soil line, enlarge plants, let sky breathe with subtle weather/sun cues
Upgrade plant illustrations into distinct species/bloom stages so streak progression is visually rewarding
Reposition stats panel to a non-occluding corner and integrate it stylistically (wooden sign, seed packet)
Add ambient motion — sway, droplets, growth transitions — to make the metaphor feel alive
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral concept outpaces behavioral clarity and reflective depth — the metaphor charms but the interaction surface and growth feedback feel underbuilt.
rationale.intent_fit: Conceptually on-brief but execution underdelivers: the garden exists, yet bloom, wilt, and watering states aren't visually differentiated enough to drive the habit loop.
